text.tspan: On this machine: SHA-256 is 1.11× to 2.08× faster than BLAKE3; BLAKE3 is 1.92× to 4.13× faster than SHA-1DC
BLAKE3 is faster at 64 B, BLAKE3 SME2 at 1 MiB; BLAKE3 is faster at 64 B, SHA-256 CommonCrypto at 1 MiB

svg.text: Line and dot: median · shaded band: minimum–maximum across 80 interleaved samples; a deeper tint or dashed outline marks a wide spread, meaning lower precision · single-threaded · lower is better

Dot shape marks the code path a contender used at that size; a ringed dot is where a new path begins · hover any dot to compare contenders and see the path · click a name at right to hide or show that contender

g.title: Click to hide or show BLAKE3

g.text: BLAKE3: blake3 1.8.7 · single-threaded; Rayon not enabled · platform NEON

g.title: Click to hide or show SHA-256

g.text: SHA-256: sha2 0.10.9 (+sha2-asm 0.6.4) · assembly backends where available (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions on AArch64)

g.title: Click to hide or show SHA-1DC

g.text: SHA-1DC: sha1-checked 0.10.0 · SHA-1 with collision detection, pure Rust (the construction git uses)

g.title: Click to hide or show BLAKE3 SME2

g.text: BLAKE3 SME2: source https://github.com/johnservil/BLAKE3 · branch sme2-bench · commit 4ca9952c8522
BLAKE3 SME2: single-threaded; SME2 kernel for groups of sixteen chunks, integer + NEON hybrid kernels below that; the benchmark stops on a CPU without SME2

g.title: Click to hide or show SHA-256 CommonCrypto

g.text: SHA-256 CommonCrypto: Apple CommonCrypto one-shot CC_SHA256 via FFI; the system's own SHA-256 (corecrypto, ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions on Apple silicon)
